report.tagline: A free app that shows the fastest way across a city using trains, buses, bikes, scooters and walking.
report.simpleSummary: Citymapper tells you how to get from A to B in a big city using public transport. It shows which bus or train to take, which carriage to sit in for the fastest exit, live arrival times, and what to do when a line is down. Londoners love it because it is often clearer than Google Maps for transit. The hard part is money: people expect a map app to be free, so Citymapper struggled to make a profit and was sold to US transit tech firm Via in 2023.

overview.whatItDoes: Citymapper is a journey planner for cities. It combines public transport, walking, cycling, bike share, scooters and taxis, and shows real-time departures and disruption. Since 2023 it is part of Via, which uses it as the rider app layer for the transit systems it builds for cities.
howItWorks: Citymapper takes open data from transport authorities like TfL, plus live arrival feeds, and builds its own route engine.
A user types a destination and sees options ranked by time, with costs, steps and live delays.
Go mode guides the user step by step, with alerts for when to get off.
The app adds small helpful details, like the best carriage to board and which station exit to use.
Money comes from in-app ads, the Citymapper Club subscription that removes ads, and licensing data and tech, now mainly through Via's business with cities.
overview.valueProposition: The fastest, clearest way to get around a big city on public transport, with live help when things go wrong.

businessModel.summary: Citymapper is free for riders and earned little money on its own: £5.8 million revenue and over £9 million loss in 2019. It made money from ads, a small subscription and licensing. Now its main business value is as part of Via, which sells transit software to cities.

revenueStreams.detail: Monthly subscription to remove ads, costing a few pounds a month.
Selling routing tech and data to companies and cities.
Via charges cities for software that includes Citymapper's tech.
Citymapper Pass (2019) and SmartRide night bus (2017 to 2019), both stopped.

businessModel.pricing: Free app. Citymapper Club costs a few pounds a month to remove ads (exact current price not confirmed).
costDrivers: Engineers and data staff for each city
Marketing to grow in new cities
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough estimate. If an active user sees ads worth maybe £1 to £2 a year, and only a small share pay for Club, average revenue per user is tiny. Each new city costs money to map and maintain. With 50 million users, 2019 revenue of £5.8 million was about 12p per user, while costs were higher. That is why Citymapper lost money and sold to Via, where it can earn indirectly through city contracts.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth and app store ratings
whatBringsUsersBack: Saved places like Home and Work
growth.moat: Citymapper's moat is its quality: clean design, accurate local data and small details like best carriage. That brand loyalty is strong in London, but it is easy for Google Maps and Apple Maps to copy features because they are already on every phone.

pmLessons: A loved product is not the same as a business. Plan how the product will make money early.
Utilities are easy to copy for big platforms that are already on every phone.
Sometimes the best buyer is a business customer, not the user. Via pays for the tech because cities pay Via.
Small delightful details like best carriage build loyalty, but they rarely pay the bills alone.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you make Citymapper profitable?
interviewQuestions.hint: List options (ads, subscriptions, ticketing, B2B licensing, city contracts), estimate revenue per user for each, and pick one with a test.

interviewQuestions.question: Citymapper versus Google Maps: why would anyone switch?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare transit detail, disruptions, design and trust; say who switches and how you would measure it.

interviewQuestions.question: What north star would you set for Citymapper?
interviewQuestions.hint: Trips completed with guidance, then break into users, trips per user, quality and revenue.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Citymapper launch in Mumbai?
interviewQuestions.hint: Consider data quality, local competitors like Chalo, user habits, revenue model and city partner needs.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you add ads without hurting retention?
interviewQuestions.hint: Choose placements outside urgent moments, test frequency, track retention and rating as guardrails.
